To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transition from the regime of slow combustion to the regime of intense one occurs when the catalyst activity increases to a certain threshold value, and that the highest filter efficiency is attained under conditions that maximize synchronization between combustion of soot in the filter porous wall and combustion the cake.

(1) a transition occurs from slow to intense combustion of soot as the catalyst activity increases; (2) the transition is associated to a change from a regime in which the catalyst activity has no significant effect on the time for regeneration of the filter, to another regime in which the filter regeneration time is substantially insensitive to the catalyst activity.

, for a catalytic diesel filter, the regeneration regime can be controlled by the catalyst activity, which can be adjusted to maximize the synchronization between the soot oxidation kinetics in the porous wall and that in the cake, thus maximizing the temperature rise and reducing the time for regeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a better understanding of the effect of catalyst activity on the combustion of the sooted filter and, in particular, on the transition between the regimes of slow and intense combustion.
the modeling of the regeneration process in a catalytic filter and, in particular, with the effect of the filter catalyst activity.
the development of a mathematical model of sooting regeneration in a catalytic filter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the catalyst activity affects regeneration dynamics of a catalytic diesel filter only if it is high enough to promote a transition from the regime of slow combustion to the regime of intense one.
the catalyst activity has a significant effect on filter regeneration only when its effect on the combustion of the cake is not negligible.
the catalyst activity affects regeneration dynamics of the catalytic diesel particlete filter only when it is high enough to affect the kinetics of combustion of the cake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the conditions investigated, the transition from the regime of slow combustion to the regime of intense one occurs when the catalyst activity reaches values in the range 1 10 4 to 1 10.

the regime of intense regeneration is established when the soot in both the porous wall and the cake are oxidized at the same time, and the temperature rise is maximized when the soot combustion in the porous wall is synchronized with combustion of the cake layer.
the regime of intense and fast combustion is established when the catalytic reaction is fast enough to allow the filter to be an effective pilot for combustion of the cake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the sake of maximizing the efficiency of the regeneration process, the catalyst activity should be tuned so as to maximize the synchronization between the two combustion processes.

, to attain a high temperature rise, the catalyst activity should be high enough to make combustion of the porous wall an effective pilot for combustion of the cake, but not so high as to make the porous walls burn out before the cake is fully consumed.
, for a given catalyst activity, it is always possible to find the optimal conditions to achieve a given temperature rise.
